name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
summary: A press where you squeeze two dumbbells together the whole time, creating constant tension in the inner chest. It works well on the floor or a bench with light weights.
setup: Lie on your back on the floor or a bench with knees bent and feet flat.
Hold two dumbbells together over your chest, with the inner ends pressed against each other and palms facing in.
Pull your shoulder blades back and keep your elbows at about 45 degrees.
execution: Squeeze the dumbbells together as hard as you can and keep that pressure throughout the set.
Press them up until your arms are straight over your chest.
Lower slowly back to your chest while still squeezing.
Stop just before the weights lose contact and repeat.
mistakes: Letting the dumbbells drift apart: use a lighter weight and focus on the squeeze.
Flaring the elbows: keep them tucked close to your torso.
Arching the lower back: keep your feet flat and ribs down.
Rushing the reps: use a slow tempo, since the tension comes from the squeeze rather than the load.
